risk_disclosed: The exact-patch interpreter pin (3.12.11) could not be fully exercised end-to-end in this local sandbox: neither `uv lock`, `uv sync --frozen`, nor `uv run` can complete at all once requires-python is tightened to ==3.12.11, because this sandbox has no such interpreter and cannot download one. All local verification therefore bypassed uv's own interpreter-discovery wrapper (invoking ocor-runtime/.venv/bin/python directly) and one lock-file line was hand-edited as a documented, justified exception (a literal copy of pyproject.toml's own field, not a resolution decision). The real qualifying gate for this change is CI, where actions/setup-python has already proven -- in every job of every PR this session (#54-60) -- that it provisions exactly Python 3.12.11 on PATH before any uv step runs. If CI's `uv sync --frozen` or `uv lock --check` fails to pick up that PATH-provided interpreter, this is the first thing to diagnose and fix at the root (e.g. UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE or an explicit --python flag pointing at the setup-python-provided binary), not to route around by loosening the pin.
